method: Every part of seed is split by its own hydration: a seed at hs% is hs/(100+hs) water and 100/(100+hs) flour, so a wetter seed carries water into the levain. With p parts of added flour per part of seed, the added-water parts q that reach a target hydration H must satisfy (q + alpha)/(p + 1 - alpha) = H/100, so q = H/100*(p + 1 - alpha) - alpha; one part of seed plus its flour and water weighs 1 + p + q, and the seed needed is the levain target divided by that. The default example builds 300 g of 100% levain from a 100% seed at 5 flour parts: 27.27 g of seed, 136.36 g of flour and 136.36 g of water, 150 g of total flour and 150 g of total water (the seed brings 13.64 g of each), a 1 : 5 : 5 feed, and 122.73 g left from a 150 g jar. When the seed sits at the same hydration as the target, q equals p*H/100, which is why a 1:5 feed at 100% reads 1 : 5 : 5. A seed wetter than the target can leave no water to add at a low flour ratio; that case is refused rather than shown as a negative weight. Inputs are limited to 1-20,000 g, 50-300% hydration for both the target and the seed, and 0.5-25 flour parts, with starter on hand optional and required to cover the seed. Fermentation mass loss, evaporation and temperature are not modelled, so the weights are the mix as built, and the page stores, uploads and transmits nothing.

sources.title: A sourdough starter is a flour-and-water culture kept by regular feeding; its hydration is the water weight as a percentage of the flour weight.
Baker's percentages express each ingredient as a percentage of total flour, which is how a feed ratio and a levain's hydration are reconciled.
